statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is a vector of length n, and for every v with 0 <= v < n, r[v] = size(v), where size is defined as follows: define depth(0)=0 and for i>=1, depth(i)=depth(parent[i])+1; for nodes x,y, y is a strict ancestor of x iff y is on the parent chain from parent[x] to 0 (i.e., either parent[x]=y, or parent[x]!=-1 and y is a strict ancestor of parent[x]); for each x with 1<=x<n, let A(x) = { y : 0<=y<n, y is a strict ancestor of x, and s[y]=s[x] }; define newpar(x) as the unique y in A(x) with maximal depth if A(x) is nonempty, and as parent[x] if A(x) is empty; the final tree has nodes {0,...,n-1}, root 0, and for each x>=1 the parent of x is newpar(x); for nodes u,v, v is an ancestor of u in the final tree (including u=v) iff v=u, or (u!=0 and v is an ancestor of newpar(u) in the final tree); finally, size(v) is the number of u with 0<=u<n such that v is an ancestor of u in the final tree.
